The Danish National Biobank (DNB) at Statens Serum Institut, is national research infrastructure, not a defined group of people: its three pillars are the Danish Biobank Register (an overview of samples held across the Danish health system and participating research biobanks), the storage facility itself, and a coordinating centre. It holds more than 25 million samples routinely collected by the health service or deposited by external and internal research projects; the home page says 'The DNB stores millions of samples. With some exemptions most samples are available for use in research projects.' (https://www.danishnationalbiobank.com/) and the about page 'The Danish National Biobank has 3 pillars: The Danish Biobank Register with detailed information about the samples available in the Danish health system and in the large research biobanks participating.' (https://www.danishnationalbiobank.com/about-dnb). The cohorts are the collections it stores (for example the Danish National Birth Cohort, COHO:0000748, a separate atlas entry, and the neonatal screening biobank used by iPSYCH, COHO:0000512), which should be curated in their own right. Caveat for the curator: COHO:0000926 (National Biobank of Korea) is typed as a cohort, a precedent for treating a national biobank hub as one; if that precedent is followed, this would be a new cohort defined from the pages above.

definition: A national consortium of existing United States pediatric longitudinal cohorts, brought together from 2016 by the National Institutes of Health's Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program, that harmonises their existing data and collects new data and biospecimens from children and their caregivers under a common protocol, extended from 2023 with new pregnancy recruitment, to study how early-life environmental exposures affect pre-, peri- and postnatal outcomes, airways, obesity, neurodevelopment and positive health.
location quote: To address these opportunities, the National Institutes of Health (NIH) Environmental influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO) Program brought together existing pediatric longitudinal observational cohorts comprising more than 200 sites in the US, including Puerto Rico, to form the national ECHO Cohort [41, 42].
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "US NIH" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry names only an agency ('US NIH'), with no website or description. Its lead investigator is the named author of the ECHO-Wide Cohort's dataset, which is cited in PMID:36963379 as 'Gillman M. Environmental Influences on Child Health Outcomes (ECHO)-Wide Cohort (Version 1) [dataset]. NICHD Data and Specimen Hub.', so the entry is taken to be the NIH's ECHO Cohort; the atlas's figures (about 105,000 enrolled, target 135,000) are of the same order as ECHO's children plus caregivers but do not match any figure read here. The identification rests on that link alone, so the curator may prefer 'unresolved'. ECHO is an aggregation: 69 existing cohorts in 31 consortia whose data are harmonised and who collect new data under a common protocol (from 2023, 'Cycle 2', it also recruits new pregnancies at Cohort Study Sites); if COHO prefers to treat the common-protocol ECHO Cohort as one cohort, the record works unchanged with type cohort. Not in COHO. 'US NIH' is kept among the acronyms because it is the atlas's name for the entry, although it names the agency, not the cohort; the curator may prefer to drop it. No members are given because the member list (Web Table 1) was not read. Could not read: Web Table 1 of PMID:36963379 (the list of the 69 ECHO cohorts, on the publisher's site), to fill members; Project Viva (COHO:0001254) is one, but no text read here states it. Not minted on 2026-09-25: the identification as the ECHO Cohort rests on the lead investigator alone, and the ECHO Cohort has its own entry; the record above is kept.

The study website now 404s; the Wayback copy was read. other synonyms: German National Cohort (NAKO)|NAKO Gesundheitsstudie|NAKO Health Study|German National Cohort health study
example quote: The German National Cohort health study (NAKO) is a prospective multicenter cohort study (N = 204,878).
definition: A multidisciplinary population-based prospective cohort of men and women aged 19 to 74 years drawn at random from the general population and examined between 2014 and 2019 at 18 study centres across Germany, with interviews, questionnaires, biomedical examinations, biosamples and whole-body magnetic resonance imaging in a subsample, followed up by questionnaires, record linkage and re-examination, to investigate the causes, early detection and prevention of common chronic and infectious diseases.

The quotes: "The Malaysian Cohort (TMC) project is a large population-based cohort study that managed to recruit 106,527 participants over a period from the year 2006 until 2012" (PMC8305012).

label: Personalized Environment and Genes Study
other synonyms: Environmental Polymorphisms Registry|Personalized Genes and Environment Study/NIEHS|Personalized Genes and Environment Study
example quote: We conducted an exposome-wide association study in the multiancestry Personalized Environment and Genes Study to assess the effects of environmental factors on type 2 diabetes.
definition: A cohort of demographically diverse adults recruited in North Carolina since 2002 by the National Institute of Environmental Health Sciences, first as the Environmental Polymorphisms Registry, who complete surveys on health, exposures, diet and lifestyle, give biological samples and are genotyped, with geocoded residential data, to study how environment, lifestyle and genes act together on disease.
location quote: PEGS participants are recruited in outpatient clinics and hospitals and at over 200 unique sites in North Carolina that include businesses, career fairs, universities, community events such as charity walks, health fairs and festivals, senior centers, sporting events, social clubs, religious institutions, and military bases.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Personalized Genes and Environment Study/NIEHS" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The NIEHS Personalized Environment and Genes Study (PEGS), which began in 2002 as the Environmental Polymorphisms Registry (EPR) and was renamed in 2022 ("The EPR was renamed the Personalized Environment and Genes Study in 2022.", PMC13216552); participants are recruited at NIEHS's Clinical Research Unit and community sites in North Carolina. The atlas swaps the words ("Personalized Genes and Environment Study"); the study's own name is "Personalized Environment and Genes Study". The atlas's enrolment period "2013:2013" does not match the papers (registry from 2002, enrolment ongoing); the definition follows the paper. EPR as an acronym is a former name; no COHO term uses EPR or PEGS.

label: Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project
example quote: we aimed to explore the non-Indigenous (European) settlement of the present NL population in unprecedented detail, studying a sample of 1807 individuals with NL ancestry from the Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project (NLGP), together with ancestry source references from Britain and Ireland.
definition: A general population cohort of adults in Newfoundland and Labrador, Canada, established by the company Sequence Bioinformatics (Sequence Bio) of St. John's and recruiting from 2019, whose participants, aged 18 and over with a valid provincial health card, were recruited at random from general practice clinics across the province and gave medical history and saliva samples for genotyping, to characterise the genetics of the province's founder population and find genetic causes of disease.
location quote: We have performed a systematic analysis of the European ancestry within the Canadian province of NL.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "Sequence Bio" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry names the company, Sequence Bio (Sequence Bioinformatics Inc., St. John's), not a cohort; its general population cohort, recruiting since 2019 (atlas), is the Newfoundland and Labrador Genome Project, which PMID:37117635 calls 'a general population cohort focused on the characterization of Newfoundland and Labrador's population (Sequence Bio Inc., 2021)'. Not in COHO (no NLGP, NL Genome or Newfoundland genome term; COHO:0000601 Newfoundland Colorectal Cancer Registry is unrelated). The company also runs later disease-specific family studies (inherited disease, familial ovarian cancer, MS, IPF) listed on its website; those are not this entry. 'Sequence Bio' is the company's name, so I did not add it as a synonym; add it only if the curator wants the atlas's tag kept. The recruitment start 2019 is from the atlas only; the definition's quote for recruitment: 'The NL Genome Project was based on the random recruitment of participants from General Practice clinics from across the province that were 18 years of age and over, possessed a valid NL health card, and provided written consent.'.

label: UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort
other synonyms: United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening|UK Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening
example quote: Using a longitudinal cohort from the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS) study, we have established that elevated autoantibodies can be detected an average of four years in advance of clinical presentation, and in some cases up to 8 years prior to clinical presentation.
definition: A cohort of postmenopausal women aged 50–74 from the general population of England, Wales and Northern Ireland, recruited in 2001–2005 to the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS), a randomised trial of ovarian cancer screening, whose donated serum samples (at recruitment and, in the multimodal screening arm, annually until 2011) and linked national health records are kept by the MRC Clinical Trials Unit at University College London as an open bioresource for studies of common diseases and disease markers.
location quote: In this trial 202,638 postmenopausal women aged 50 and above were recruited through thirteen UK centres between 2001 and 2005.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "UKCTOCS Longitudinal Women's Cohort (UKLWC)" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The UKLWC is the bioresource of the women of the UKCTOCS ovarian cancer screening trial: the UCL ICTU page says 'UKLWC is the bioresource created during the course of the United Kingdom Collaborative Trial of Ovarian Cancer Screening (UKCTOCS) as a result of participants (202,280 postmenopausal women from the general population in England, Wales and Northern Ireland) donating their samples and data for use in secondary studies.' The trial randomised 202,638 women; the UKLWC is the 202,280 who donated, so the trial and the UKLWC are the same people bar withdrawals, and neither is in COHO (no UKCTOCS, UKLWC or ovarian screening trial term). I propose one term, labelled with the entry's own name, carrying the trial's name and acronym as synonyms, since papers name it as UKCTOCS; a curator who prefers two terms would mint UKCTOCS and make the UKLWC isSubCohortOf it. The atlas's separate entry 'UCL, UK' (same lead investigator, enrolment 2001–2005, 202,638) is this same cohort.

IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "South(east) Asian Cohorts" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The atlas entry is a collective label ('South(east) Asian Cohorts', plural; region 'Southeastern Asia'; website the Cambridge Cardiovascular Epidemiology Unit (CEU); enrolment from 2010, 80,000 of a target 120,000), not the name of a cohort, and no source I found defines it. The CEU's South Asian studies are the Bangladesh Risk of Acute Vascular Events Study (BRAVE, established 2011; COHO:0001546), the Pakistan Risk Of Myocardial Infarction Study (PROMIS; COHO:0000169) and the BangladEsh Longitudinal Investigation of Emerging Vascular Events (BELIEVE, launched 2016, about 74,000 participants per the CEU Global Health page; not in COHO). The numbers fit BRAVE plus BELIEVE, which would make this an umbrella of CEU cohorts, but nothing says so, and the start year 2010 and 'Southeastern Asia' fit neither exactly. Not minted as an aggregation for want of a source naming it and its members; BELIEVE (https://www.phpc.cam.ac.uk/research/departmental-research-units/ceu/global-health, cohort profile PMC11784369) is a candidate new cohort in its own right. The automatic 'exact' match to COHO:0001477 (Early Treatment of Atrial Fibrillation for Stroke Prevention Trial) is spurious (it matched the '(east)' in the name to that trial's acronym EAST).

label: Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System
example quote: We leveraged the Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System of 90 257 households and asked whether they had a case of tungiasis in the household at interview during three survey rounds of routine surveys, undertaken between May 2021 and May 2022.
definition: A population cohort of the residents of a defined area around Kilifi on the Indian Ocean coast of Kenya, established in 2000 by the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme with a census and followed by regular household visits recording births, pregnancies, migrations and deaths, with residents' admissions to Kilifi District Hospital linked to the population register, to measure the incidence of local diseases, evaluate community interventions against infectious diseases and provide a sampling frame for epidemiological studies.
location quote: The Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System (KHDSS), located on the Indian Ocean coast of Kenya, was established in 2000 as a record of births, pregnancies, migration events and deaths and is maintained by 4-monthly household visits.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "KEMRI-Wellcome" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The entry names the institution, the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kilifi, Kenya, not a cohort; the atlas gives no description, but its population of 300,000 under the programme's director fits the programme's population cohort, the Kilifi Health and Demographic Surveillance System ('The KHDSS has 260 000 residents' in 2012, PMID:22544844), which the profile says 'is nested in the KEMRI-Wellcome Trust Research Programme in Kilifi'. The atlas's start year 2003 does not match (census September 2000 to October 2001; pregnancy surveillance from March 2003), so the identification rests on the population size and host, not on an explicit statement; the curator may want IHCC to confirm. An HDSS population is modelled as a cohort in COHO (compare COHO:0000912, Agincourt HDSS). Not in COHO: no Kilifi, KHDSS or KEMRI term. 'KEMRI-Wellcome' is an institution's name and is not proposed as a synonym.

The entry names an institution, Johns Hopkins University, with the country South Korea, enrolment from 2002 and 800,000 participants; the atlas gives no description. This identification rests on those facts, not on a statement naming the atlas entry; the Korean Cancer Prevention Study-II Biobank (COHO:0000486), recruited in 2004–2013 per its COHO definition, fits the start year less well. KSHS is not in COHO (no Kangbuk or KSHS term). 'Johns Hopkins University' is an institution's name and is not proposed as a synonym. example quote: Between 1985 and 2001, 167 371 adult Vorarlberg residents were enrolled in the VHM&PP Study Cohort after signing an informed consent to store and process personal data (height, weight, smoking and other factors).
definition: A population-based cohort of adult residents of Vorarlberg, the westernmost province of Austria, enrolled from 1985 through a routine risk-factor surveillance and prevention programme run by the Agency for Social and Preventive Medicine, in which local physicians carried out a physical examination, blood test and consultation, and followed by linkage to the Vorarlberg cancer registry and death index to study metabolic and other risk factors for cancer, cardiovascular disease and mortality.
location quote: The Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Promotion Program (VHM&PP) is carried out in Vorarlberg, the westernmost province of Austria.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "VHM&PP" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. VHM&PP is the Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention (also written Promotion) Programme, a population-based cohort in Austria led from the Medical University of Innsbruck (the atlas lead is its long-standing investigator). The atlas gives the country as Germany, which is wrong: every source places it in Vorarlberg, Austria. The expansion of the acronym differs between papers ('Prevention Programme' in the Me-Can cohort profile, 'Promotion Program' in the Br J Cancer paper); I took the Me-Can form as label and kept the other as a synonym. It is one of the cohorts of the Metabolic syndrome and Cancer project (Me-Can: 'in Austria, the Vorarlberg Health Monitoring and Prevention Programme (VHM&PP)', PMID:19380371), which has no COHO term, so no parent is given. It also contributed to ESCAPE/ELAPSE air-pollution pools, which are not in COHO either.
IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "UK Biobank" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), matched to the term by name on 2026-09-25; the atlas's name for it is added as a synonym.

label: 45 and Up Study
example quote: The Sax Institute's 45 and Up Study is a large-scale Australian cohort study of 267 151 men and women aged 45 years and over, randomly sampled from the general population of New South Wales (NSW), Australia.
definition: A prospective population-based cohort of men and women aged 45 years and over in New South Wales, Australia, randomly sampled from the Medicare enrolment database and recruited by postal questionnaire in 2005–2009 by the Sax Institute, with oversampling of people aged 80 and over and of rural and remote residents, repeated follow-up surveys, biospecimen sub-studies and routine linkage to mortality, hospital, pharmaceutical and other health records, as a resource for research on health and ageing.
location quote: The 45 and Up Study (‘the Study’) recruited 267 357 participants aged ≥45 years from New South Wales, Australia between 2005 and 2009 as a resource for researchers and policy makers to source evidence to support better health and ageing.
note: IHCC Cohort Atlas entry "45 and Up Study" (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), checked against its sources on 2026-09-25. The 45 and Up Study is a single, well-described prospective cohort run by the Sax Institute in New South Wales (atlas lead is the Sax Institute's lead on the update paper; 267,000 enrolled 2005-2009 matches '267 357 participants'). Nothing in COHO matches it (no label, synonym or acronym containing '45 and Up', 'Sax' or a New South Wales ageing cohort). The study has no acronym of its own; the atlas name is the label. The definition is written from the 2022 update alone; the original 2008 profile (PMID:17881411) was requested but not read. Could not read: PMID:17881411 (original cohort profile; not needed for any quote).

label: International Health Cohorts Consortium
other synonyms: International HundredK+ Cohorts Consortium|International Hundred K+ Cohorts Consortium|International Hundred Thousand Plus Cohort Consortium
example quote: As a collaboration model of the International Hundred K+ Cohorts Consortium (IHCC), we endeavored to develop a globally applicable trans‐ethnic PRS for body mass index (BMI) through this relatively new international effort.
definition: An international consortium of large population cohorts, established in 2018 to work beyond the constraints of individual health and population cohorts, whose members are chosen for size, longitudinal health follow-up, broad participant selection, biological sample collection and a commitment to data sharing, and which maintains the IHCC Cohort Atlas, a directory of the data its member cohorts hold.
note: The consortium that lists the cohorts of the IHCC Cohort Atlas (https://atlas.ihccglobal.org/), minted 2026-09-25 so that each listed cohort can be recorded as its member; its names are those its papers use (PMID:40841586, PMID:37337639), the earlier "International HundredK+ Cohorts Consortium" among them. The acronym IHCC is shared with the International Hereditary Cancer Centre (COHO:0001909).
